TEDDEPICS · FIELD PHOTOGRAPHY VOL. II · SHOOT PLANNING DIVISION

Every circuit I can stand beside, and exactly when.

Twenty-three circuits on the Nordic map, from Åsum to Vuollerim. Eight dates that are actually mine. Each one measured to the metre — lap length, corner count, the longest straight you can hold focus down — before I ever put a boot in the gravel.

— DESCEND THE CATALOGUE
01MANDATE
MEASURED GEOMETRY · STANDING ORDER

You get one pass at the light.

A race weekend does not repeat. The sun crosses the main straight once at that angle, the field runs three-wide into that corner once, and if you were still walking back to the car you did not shoot it. So the planning happens here, weeks early, in a document that knows where every apex actually is.

None of this is guesswork about the racing. It is guesswork about me — where I will be standing, what focal length reaches, which fence has a hole in it. The circuit itself is the one part of the problem that holds still, so the circuit is the part I measured.

Method

Every lap length, corner count and longest straight on this page is computed from a traced centreline — OpenStreetMap ways and satellite-verified fits carried over from Field Atlas 1.x — resampled to eight-metre steps, then walked for heading change.

Confidence

Corner counts are a reading, not a rulebook. A run of same-signed turn above 32° counts once, so sweepers score one and chicanes score two. Where a venue had no geo fit the figure is scaled from the hand trace and labelled est. — assume the last digit is a hope.

Provenance

Season dates, venues and club names are mastered in Field Atlas 1.x and pulled in by trace/extract.py. This page never invents a date. If it is wrong here it is wrong there, and there is where it gets fixed.

COMPETITION CIRCUITS · REFERENCE LAYER

Every Swedish competition karting circuit I could shoot but have not booked. No countdown, no plan — a reference layer, sorted north to south, so a free weekend has somewhere to go.
